---
title: "comparing_income_methods"
output: html_document
---

```{r}
# Libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(scales)
library(showtext)
font_add_google("Open Sans", "Open Sans")
font_add_google("PT Serif", "Georgia") 
showtext_auto()

# 1. Load the data
income_comp <- read_xlsx("../data/processed/median_income_comparison.xlsx") %>%
  rename(Original = original)

# 2. Prepare the data for plotting
income_comp_sorted <- income_comp %>%
  arrange(Original) %>%
  mutate(councildist = factor(councildist, levels = councildist))

income_long <- income_comp_sorted %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Original, PUMS, NYHC),
    names_to = "Method",
    values_to = "Income"
  ) %>%
  mutate(Method = factor(Method, levels = c("Original", "NYHC", "PUMS"),
                         labels = c("Our Method (CT Population-Weighted)", 
                                    "NYHC (Areal Overlap)", 
                                    "PUMS (Synthetic Downscaling)")))

# 3. Build the Dumbbell Plot
comparison_plot <- ggplot(income_long, aes(x = Income, y = councildist)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = councildist), color = "gray75", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(color = Method), size = 3.5, alpha = 0.9) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Our Method (CT Population-Weighted)" = "#2f56a6", # Blue
    "NYHC (Areal Overlap)" = "#4f9560",                # Green
    "PUMS (Synthetic Downscaling)" = "#e91e63"         # Pink
  )) +
  
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::dollar_format(), breaks = seq(30000, 180000, by = 25000)) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Comparing Income Aggregation Methods",
    subtitle = "Sorted from lowest to highest income.",
    x = "Estimated Median Household Income",
    y = "Council District (Ranked by Income Level)",
    caption = "Source: ACS 5-Year Estimates. Original, PUMS, and NYHC Methodologies."
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    text = element_text(family = "Open Sans"),
    plot.title = element_text(family = "Georgia", size = 16, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(family = "Georgia", size = 11, margin = margin(b = 15), color = "gray30"),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), # Remove horizontal grid lines to make the dumbbell lines pop
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8, color = "gray20"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold")
  )

# 4. Display and Save
print(comparison_plot)

ggsave(comparison_plot, filename = "../figures2/median_income_methodology_comparison.png", 
       units = "in", width = 10, height = 12, dpi = 300)
```

```{r}
# 1. Load data and divide into 3 Income Tiers
income_comp <- read_xlsx("../data/processed/median_income_comparison.xlsx") %>%
  rename(Original = original) %>%
  # Rank based on our method
  mutate(Rank = rank(Original, ties.method = "first")) %>%
  mutate(
    Tier = case_when(
      Rank <= 17 ~ "Low Income Districts\n(Bottom Third)",
      Rank <= 34 ~ "Mid Income Districts\n(Middle Third)",
      TRUE       ~ "High Income Districts\n(Top Third)"
    ),
    # Lock the order of the tiers for the plot
    Tier = factor(Tier, levels = c("Low Income Districts\n(Bottom Third)", 
                                   "Mid Income Districts\n(Middle Third)", 
                                   "High Income Districts\n(Top Third)"))
  )

# 2. Calculate the average estimate for each method within each tier
tier_summary <- income_comp %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Original, PUMS, NYHC),
    names_to = "Method",
    values_to = "Income"
  ) %>%
  group_by(Tier, Method) %>%
  summarize(Avg_Income = mean(Income, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(Method = factor(Method, levels = c("Original", "NYHC", "PUMS"),
                         labels = c("Our Method (CT Pop-Weighted)", 
                                    "NYHC (Areal Overlap)", 
                                    "PUMS (Synthetic Downscaling)")))

# 3. Build the Grouped Bar Chart
summary_plot <- ggplot(tier_summary, aes(x = Tier, y = Avg_Income, fill = Method)) +
    geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7, alpha = 0.9) +
    geom_text(aes(label = scales::dollar(round(Avg_Income, 0))), 
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), 
            vjust = -0.5, family = "Open Sans", size = 3.5, fontface = "bold", color = "gray20") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "Our Method (CT Pop-Weighted)" = "#2f56a6", # Blue
    "NYHC (Areal Overlap)" = "#4f9560",         # Green
    "PUMS (Synthetic Downscaling)" = "#e91e63"  # Pink
  )) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::dollar_format(), 
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) + # Give breathing room at the top for labels
  labs(
    title = "Methodology Comparison by District Wealth",
    subtitle = "Average estimated median income across the three methods, grouped by district income tiers.",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Average Estimated Median Income",
    caption = "Source: ACS 5-Year Estimates. Original, PUMS, and NYHC Methodologies."
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    text = element_text(family = "Open Sans"),
    plot.title = element_text(family = "Georgia", size = 16, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(family = "Georgia", size = 11, margin = margin(b = 15), color = "gray30"),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(), # Remove vertical grid lines
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", color = "black"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10, color = "gray30"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold", margin = margin(r = 10))
  )

# 4. Display and Save
print(summary_plot)

ggsave(summary_plot, filename = "../figures2/income_summary_by_tier.png", 
       units = "in", width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```
